feature: defect-scan.yml / production/bible/defect_scan.py (free-defect-scan-v1): detector only, WARN / INFO, never an approval
executor: Claude (research subagent); measured on a 4-CPU / 15 GB Linux sandbox with the public release copy of the master; no human listening by this executor; not yet run on GitHub Actions

master.name: Babel long (pilot-020, genesis-10-11-long)
master.source: public release asset bible-genesis-10-11-long-sha256-0386d34a....mp4 (already public on YouTube)
master.owner_verdict: owner listened and approved; 00:55 'mighty', 02:17-02:22 b-brick line and 06:51 'babel' are known ASR false alarms

warn: 01:10 garbled_word sentence 21: both small.en and medium.en heard 'a wretch and a cad' for 'Erech, and Accad' (a name pronunciation for the reviewer; not one of the known points)

known_points.06:51 babel: INFO only (medium.en heard it in its window; Soundex match)

result.info: 5 garbled_word INFO (ASR slips a window decode heard: 06:51, 06:52, 07:11, 07:30 Haran, 07:33) + the sync note
result.loudness: no jump; largest short-term change 3.0 LU per s against the 8 LU threshold
result.clash: 125 sentences measured on separated stems: voice over music min 6.5 dB, median 8.1 dB; INFO below 5 dB, WARN below 3 dB: none
result.picture: 14,489 frames, no one-frame flash, no black, no freeze

runtime.projection: about 35 min for a 15 min master and 47 min for 20 min on a 4-vCPU runner (timeout 150 min); separation=false saves about 75 s per minute

fixes_found_by_calibration: Demucs with separate.py-style mean/std normalisation returned voice = music (0 dB on all 125 sentences); the raw mix separates (+6.5 to +18.3 dB), so the mix goes in unnormalised, 60 s per call
a 1 s window ('Babel.') decoded empty: windows are at least 4 s
proper names spelled differently by the ASR ('Beybell', 'heron') count as heard when Soundex matches
torch 2.6 refused the local Demucs file (weights_only); the hash-verified file is placed in torch.hub's cache instead

licenses.demucs 4.0.1 + htdemucs: MIT (code; weights released in the same MIT repository, archived 2025-01-01). Training data included MUSDB18-HQ, itself research-licensed: the stems are a measurement here, never published content
licenses.ffmpeg: LGPL/GPL build from Ubuntu, used as a tool

limits: one approved master; no defective master yet, so recall is unmeasured; thresholds are provisional; lip-sync is not judged; a WARN is a question for the listening reviewer, never a refusal
next: run defect-scan.yml on Actions on the same sha256 (runtime on the real runner), then on a master with a known defect (or a deliberately damaged copy) to measure recall before relying on it
